answer: Sybil resistance rests on non-transferable stake escrow: an identity must park a minimum of copper-denominated tokens before its first attestation counts, and escrow binds to the operator, not the key pair. Cloning a thousand keys is cheap; funding a thousand escrows is not, since each needs a distinct verified funding path and stays locked through a cooldown. When a fresh cluster votes together, funding-graph analysis traces them to one pool and slashes it, so an attacker burns stake times cluster size attempting it, then loses it. Each identity is a jetty before docking; a lotus needs one.
